I build past the demo, with user workflows, data and deployment. Right now I’m deepening my Luau, learning data structures and algorithms in C++, and building a new horror game.

projects.title: Student Codex
projects.description: Assignments, projects and exams reach students through Google Classroom, group chats and in-class announcements, so deadlines pile up unseen. Student Codex is an Android-first workload platform: it syncs Google Classroom coursework read-only, lets students add everything else by hand, and gives teachers a calendar view of the combined workload.

items: A teacher dashboard with calendars and filters by course, section, year level and program.
A Supabase backend on PostgreSQL, with migration-based schema, Row Level Security policies and authorization tests.
Source identifiers on synced coursework prevent duplicate records.

Built every piece of the software in two days — the Android app, the Supabase/PostgreSQL database, the Google Classroom sync and the teacher dashboard — while my two teammates wrote the paper and slides. I then delivered the main presentation and defended the architecture in the judges’ technical Q&A, from the Classroom integration and JSON processing to the PostgreSQL structure and duplicate prevention.
details.facts: 2nd place of 7 teams · ParSU IGNITE CryptCamp Hackathon · Nov 2026

projects.title: Pamanang Bayan
projects.description: A platform for preserving and sharing Indigenous knowledge across the Philippines: stories, oral histories, languages and landmarks on a map, built around consent and responsible representation.

items: Cultural landmarks mapped with Leaflet and OpenStreetMap.
Firebase authentication with role-based content management, moderation and reporting.
A Node and Express backend with PostgreSQL, deployed on Vercel and Render.
Installable as a Progressive Web App.

projects.title: Bindery
projects.description: Upload documents, set their exact order, preview them full screen, then download one combined file. Temporary uploads are cleaned up automatically.

items: Handles PDF, Word, PowerPoint, ODT, RTF and plain text.
Docker packages the system’s plugins and tools for the desktop build.
Built around predictable ordering and previewing before output.
A desktop version for local PDF work is part of the concept.

projects.title: Coffee++
projects.description: A digital menu and order system for a student-organization booth. Customers order from a QR menu, the booth tracks waiting and served orders, and the admin side reports sales.

items: Hot and cold options with product images, prices and optional GCash QR payment details.
An order dashboard with sales and profit analytics and Excel-compatible export.
The customer site is separate from the local admin and scanning workflow.

projects.title: SPECS App Store
projects.description: A platform where the Computer Science community showcases student-built apps — listings, submissions, voting and comments. Built together with another developer.

items: A discovery page with student application listings and descriptions.
Built security and authentication: Google OAuth sign-in, Cloudflare Turnstile captcha, sensitive-link blocking and the privacy policy.
Leaderboards, comments and user profiles on Supabase/PostgreSQL, with Google Cloud APIs.
186 automated tests in Vitest; deployed on Vercel.
Large downloads are linked externally to stay within free hosting limits.

projects.title: AV Fitness Gym
projects.description: A website for AV Fitness Gym with a calm, dim-lit look in black, white and dark gray, built around the gym’s own logo. It’s still in planning, so it isn’t live yet.

items: Comfortable, smooth and aesthetic, with dim lighting.
Status: planning. Pages and features will be listed once they’re built and verified.

projects.title: JARVIS
projects.description: A voice-first assistant that runs on local models. Every command passes a six-layer pipeline, and a validation gate checks the small model’s tool pick before anything executes.

items: A small model dispatches simple tools; a larger one handles multi-step chains.
Multi-command splitting with one combined spoken reply.
A calibration tool tunes routing thresholds from its own logs.
Faster-Whisper in, Piper out. Core features need no cloud.

projects.title: Mini IDE
projects.description: An AI code editor that runs entirely on my machine. It edits several files at once, plans across the whole workspace, and shows each agent’s reasoning as it works.

items: Surgical search/replace edits instead of whole-file rewrites.
FAISS retrieval gives it awareness of the codebase.
Critic, security and performance agents review every change.

projects.title: AfterHours
projects.description: An open-world hangout with exploration, parkour, a SkyWars mode and a singing stage. Inventory and the item shop persist across sessions. One of three games I’ve designed and published on Roblox.

items: Rafts on waypoint paths, rope swings, checkpoints and a two-mode carry system.
The stage mic runs a full audio chain, from compressor to reverb, with eight vocal presets.
Ten-player SkyWars matchmaking and a day/night cycle.
details.facts: 12 checkpoints · 9 rafts · 11 rope swings · 8 vocal presets

projects.title: Horror game
projects.description: Something is stalking you, and it only moves when nobody is looking. One to five players race to collect five keys and escape.

items: First-person only, with a minimal dot crosshair.
The monster follows footprint and scent trails to hunt players it cannot see.
Team sizes from solo to five, plus a scary start page and settings menu.
